diagram_math_checks.result: Both panels act on C^2 tensor C^2 with ordered wires q1,q0 and computational basis 00,01,10,11. H(q1)=H tensor I and H(q0)=I tensor H. The lower filled control and upper P2=diag(1,i) box act as diag(1,1,1,i), exactly L1 and the gate-cost-model definition. No ancilla is depicted.

The exact panel reads H(q1), CP2(q0,q1), H(q0), SWAP, at increasing horizontal positions 0.9,2.1,3.3,4.6. This is Example line 33, L2 and exact-binary-QFT algorithm step 1 for n=2 followed by its reversal step 2. The operator is S(I tensor H) CP2 (H tensor I). Independent finite complex matrix multiplication agrees with the displayed positive-sign F4+ to maximum entrywise floating error 1.1102230246251565e-16; Verification 1.1 supplies the independent exact basis-column argument.

The second panel has H(q1), H(q0), SWAP at the same remaining horizontal positions and no CP2 box/control/connector. Since s=2>m=1, this is exactly the deletion rule in truncated-binary-QFT and L2. It has 3 ideal gates, versus 4 above, agreeing with Example and Verification 3.1. The omitted CP2-I acts only on |11> with coefficient i-1, of magnitude sqrt(2), matching Verification 1.2.

Each pair of joined crosses is a SWAP between the two displayed wires, not crossed trajectories that silently relabel the wires. S=P exchanges basis positions 01 and 10, fixes 00 and 11, and squares to I by L4. Reversing both input and output displayed order therefore gives P F4+ P, not just P F4+ or F4+ P. Independent row/column permutation reproduces exactly the second displayed matrix, as in Verification 2.1. The text explicitly distinguishes this coordinate change from chronological gates.
All original Example, Facts and Verification bytes are retained. The final Remarks calls the figures illustrations only; no proof step uses them.
